contexts.text: Plagues = vastations.
To be smitten with plagues () = to be destroyed.
Plague of horse, mule, camel, and donkey () = intellectual things affected with plagues. AC 3048:7.
All the captivities and plagues of the Israelites were to the end that...
The process of their devastation is described by the eleven plagues (of Egypt).
I will send all My plagues () = that all the coming evils would rush on them together. Plagues = evils.
It is according to order that one plague should follow another; and that the evil should thus be successively cast down into Hell. Explained.
The miracles, or plagues, in Egypt, = falsities and evils... Each one = some kind of falsity and evil.
Yet one plague [more] () = the last of vastation.
No plague of the destroyer upon you () = that damnation from Hell shall not inflow.
To inflict a plague upon Egypt () = damnation to those who have been in faith separated from charity. AC 7930. AC 7941.
Hurt a woman with child () = the injuring of the good which is from truth.
Wound is predicated of the injuring of good; and plague, of the injuring of truth. Illustrated.

Stripe for stripe () = something of affection in the Intellectual which is extinguished or injured. Explained... Stripe, in the Original, is expressed by a word which means gore... Hence stripe = truth injured or extinguished. This is signified by the plagues in the Apocalypse, etc.; and by the wounds inflicted on the man who fell among thieves ()... The Samaritan's binding up his wounds = the healing of that injured affection. (Compare AE 444:14.)
Under Ox, see this reference.
The injury remains there, like a scar...
The stroke of their wound () = the evil of life thence.
Forty stripes () = the penalty to the full.
A plague () = the penalty of evil.

There are three plagues which follow those who attribute to themselves the truths of faith and goods of love... Enumerated... These three penalties are signified by the three plagues which were proposed to David. Enumerated, Explained.
(The origin of the plagues of Egypt.)
Who were not killed by these plagues () = those not so spiritually dead from visionary reasonings, and from the love of self, the conceit of Own intelligence, and from the concupiscences thence.
That plagues = spiritual plagues. Illustrated.
To smite the earth with every plague () = to bring ruin upon the Church by falsities and evils of every kind.
The plagues (of Egypt) significative of the cupidities of the natural man separated from the spiritual. Enumerated.
His wound of death was healed () = the cure of that head of doctrine... AE 786.

The seven last plagues () = the evils and falsities in the Church, such as are in its last state... Plagues = evils of love, and falsities of faith; for they are the things described in the following chapter. Enumerated. AR 670.
That plagues = spiritual plagues, which affect men as to their souls... and which are evils and falsities. Illustrated.
The plagues of Egypt, which were in part like those described here = nothing else than evils and falsities.
The seven plagues () = all evils and falsities, universally understood.
The seven plagues of the seven Angels () = the evils and falsities which devastate the Church and make an end of it.
To have Power over these plagues () = that from Him inflow all the good of love and truth of faith by which evils and falsities are removed.

The plague of it was exceeding great () = on account of those direful and atrocious falsities from confirming the dogma of justification by faith alone. ( = the total destruction of genuine truth. Explained. AE 1028.)
That ye receive not of her plagues () = lest they perish; for by plagues are signified evils and falsities; and at the same time destruction by them.
In one day shall her plagues come () = at the time of the Last Judgment the penalties of the evils which they have done will return upon them. Enumerated, Explained. AE 1124.
God shall add unto him the plagues which are written in this book () = that (such) cannot but perish from the falsities and evils which are signified by the plagues described in this book.

In seven chapters in the Apocalypse is described the devastation of the present Church, in like manner as is described that of Egypt; and both are described by similar plagues, each of which signifies some falsity which promoted its devastation even to destruction. (Parallel between the plagues of Egypt and those of the Apocalypse.)
To beat () = to injure the mind and the spiritual life with falsities. (Compare AE 584:end.)
Like things are signified by the plagues of Egypt as by (these) plagues in the Apocalypse; for by... the plagues of Egypt are signified those changes which precede the Last Judgment...
The Egyptian plagues = spiritual plagues...

Who were not killed in these plagues = who had not perished from the above-named cupidities... These are called plagues, because by plagues, in the Word, are signified such things as destroy the Spiritual life with man, and consequently the Church; consequently, which induce (spiritual) death; and which, in sum, relate to the cupidities springing from the loves of self and of the world... Illustrated.
As reformation succeeds punishment, it is said that he shall not be smitten with many stripes ().
To smite the earth with every plague = that the Church with them perishes through the concupiscences of evil.
The plagues of Egypt = the vastation of the natural man as to all the truths and goods of the Church. Enumerated.
Wound of death = discordance with the Word.
The seven last plagues = the evils and falsities in the complex which completely devastate the Church. AE 949. AE 957.
Wound, and scar, and recent sore () the evils of the will, and the derivative falsities of the thought, continually more.
The miracles in Egypt, which were so many plagues, and are also called diseases, = so many infesting evils and falsities, devastating and destroying the Church which is with spiritual men.
Having Power over these plagues = no fear of the Last Judgment... and of the damnation and punishment of the evils and derivative falsities which have devastated the Church.
